Coverage is pure-function tests of shapers (mobile-booking-form, mobile-flash, mobile-goods, mobile-onboarding, mobile-settings, mobile-travel) plus exactly one behavioural test: e2e 'artist A cannot approve artist B's request via the mobile API shape'. | unknown |
| Appointment payment settlement (P9 slice A4): convergence, idempotency and event ordering / money | substantial | A third pass over the same code, deliberately not re-running the author's or the tester's scenarios. Read in full: 0128_payment_settlement.sql, appointment-payment-settlement.ts, api/stripe/appointment-webhook/route.ts, the transition table, PAYABLE set, apportionCollection and checkAllocation in packages/shared, and the constraint and trigger sections of 0125 and 0127. Then twelve probes with MY OWN fixtures, driven against the local stack through the real service client, the real RPC and (for the HTTP question) the real route with real HMAC verification. Both probe files were deleted after the run; nothing was left in the repository. WHAT HELD UP, each executed. (1) NOTHING ADDS A DELTA. Every write to payment_allocations was enumerated by grep: exactly two, the settle path's fresh one-statement insert and 0128's `on conflict on constraint payment_allocations_unique do update set amount_minor = excluded.amount_minor`. The sequence 3000, 5000, 3000-out-of-order, 5000, 5000 produced converged/converged/stale/unchanged/unchanged with exactly ONE refund_adjustment row throughout and a final -5000. (2) REDELIVERY CANNOT DOUBLE-ALLOCATE. The same succeeded event five times (three sequential, then two concurrent from two backends) left 2 rows with the SAME row ids as the first delivery and a sum of 10000; a pair of concurrent FIRST deliveries produced settled + already_settled and 1 row, with neither call failing. (3) THE CONVERGE IS GENUINELY UNDER A ROW LOCK. With a newer event holding the payment_collections row in an open transaction, the older call BLOCKED (pg_blocking_pids count 1, 1231ms) and answered `stale` after re-reading; the stored total stayed at the newer 7000. The lock-first / re-check-in-a-later-statement shape of 0124 and 0125 is correctly implemented here. (4) THE UNKNOWN-INTENT PATH DOES NOT 500. Over real HTTP: a charge.refunded for an intent no payment request has ever claimed answered 200 `not_ours`; a claimed-but-unsettled intent answered 500 while the event was young and 200 once it aged past the one-hour bound. That is the correct shape for BILL-ENT-002. (5) ALLOCATION INTEGRITY HOLDS. A partial 3333 of a 11000 basket containing a discount line allocated to full_price=3030, discount=-454, physical_goods=757, summing exactly to 3333, with checkAllocation running BEFORE the insert; a second collection on the same request moved partially_paid then paid correctly. Reasoned, not just executed: a component cannot silently go missing, because one row is emitted per frozen line and checkAllocation refuses the set unless the gross components sum to what Stripe collected. (6) THE BACKWARD-WALK GUARD ON THE SETTLE PATH HOLDS. With the request at `refunded` and at `partially_refunded`, a redelivered succeeded returned already_settled / statusMovedTo null and changed nothing. | no |
| Appointment payment settlement: the webhook endpoint, the three cores, and the refund convergence RPC (P9 slice A4) / money | substantial | A4 shipped with no test of any kind; its own behavioural evidence came from throwaway probes that were deleted. This pass turned that into a gate: apps/web/tests/db/appointment-payment-settlement.test.ts, 26 tests (25 passing plus one documented `it.fails` tripwire), which took the db suite from 191 to 217. WHAT IS REAL IN IT: the local Postgres with its constraints, triggers, grants and RLS; the `converge_payment_refund` RPC from 0128; the RLS-bypassing service client the cores are handed in production; the artist's own anon-key client holding a real JWT; the three settlement cores; and the webhook route driven end to end through Stripe's REAL HMAC verification (`webhooks.generateTestHeaderString`), so the HTTP status codes asserted are the ones a Stripe delivery would receive. WHAT IS NOT REAL: the Stripe API (no key is reachable; event payloads are hand-built to the documented shape). OBLIGATIONS DISCHARGED, one block each: redelivery is a no-op (one allocation set, one state move, the SAME row ids, and the fee actuals caught up after a delivery that died between the two writes); an older event never overwrites newer state (both for the request status and for a superseded intent); refund convergence (3000 then 5000 is 5000 in ONE row, a late older 3000 answers `stale` and does not reduce it, a plain redelivery answers `unchanged`, an over-refund clamps at the collected total and the net never goes negative); partial payment (proportional shares summing to exactly what Stripe moved, line-attributed rows, and A1's `outstandingBalance` recomputed FROM DISK at 4000/6000 then 10000/0); mixed service and goods (bases 9000 and 4500 disjoint, tip, tax and shipping in neither, and on a half collection the bases are 4500 and 2250 rather than the frozen basket's 13500); an unknown intent (real 200 with nothing written, a real 500 while the settlement may still arrive, and a real 200 once the retry window has passed, which is the BILL-ENT-002 bound); a failed payment (the artist's OWN client is silently refused from `payment_processing`, 0 rows and no error, and succeeds from `failed`, which is the recourse property exercised rather than asserted from a constant); forgery (allocation INSERT 42501 by privilege, the converge RPC 42501 by grant with a service-role positive control, and the fee actuals unchanged); and concurrency (two backends, `pg_blocking_pids` proving contention, the older event losing to the newer under the row lock, and a control that still converges afterwards). MUTATION CAMPAIGN, 26 mutations, one per test, each stated before it was run, applied, run BY NAME with --reporter=verbose, restored, and re-run green. 25 killed their test; the reds are logged verbatim in the file header. ONE CAME BACK GREEN AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: the refund-delta mutation does not kill the identical-deliveries race, because the loser short-circuits on `v_target = v_recorded` before the arithmetic runs. Two EXISTING tests were also checked for vacuity: A4's addition to appointment-payments-convergence.test.ts is NOT vacuous (removing 0128 from its repair run goes red naming `payment_collections_bases_check` and `payment_collections_fee_minor_check`), and the A3 tripwire A4 converted from `it.fails` to `it` still discriminates (reverting the quote to the frozen basket turns it red at 600 <= 100). FULL GATE after the change: typecheck clean, lint 0 errors and the same 16 pre-existing warnings, unit 2375 unchanged, db 216 passed plus 1 expected fail. | no |

| Mobile JSON API routes and web server actions: authentication, ownership scoping, input validation, error handling, IDOR and cache revalidation / authz | substantial | SCOPE AS ASSIGNED, all read in full: 17 mobile route files (booking-form + fields + fields/[id] + confirmation, goods + [id] + [id]/status + collections + discounts, projects + [id], settings/appearance + email-templates + hub + slug, travel/studios + travel/trips) and 18 server-action files ((artist) bookings/booking-form, bookings/form, bookings/books, bookings/projects, bookings/settings, goods, goods/collections, goods/discounts, settings/appearance, settings/books, settings/plan, settings/profile/slug-actions, studio; plus [slug], [slug]/project, request/[token], legal/report, (map)/map). Because most actions are thin wrappers, the shared cores they delegate to were read too and are the substantive part of the coverage: lib/server/mobile-auth.ts, collections.ts, discount-write.ts, projects.ts, goods-variants.ts, slug-rename.ts, appearance-write.ts, confirmation-write.ts, map-watch.ts, plus lib/ratelimit.ts, lib/image-guard.ts, lib/image-processing.ts and lib/mobile-goods.ts. LIMB 1, AUTHENTICATION — CLEAN, no exceptions. All 17 mobile routes begin with `requireMobileUser(req)` and return before touching data on failure. All 18 action files resolve the user through the cookie client and refuse when absent. requireMobileUser itself (mobile-auth.ts:28-75) validates the bearer token via supabase.auth.getUser, builds an RLS-SCOPED anon-key client rather than a service client, and adds a suspension gate that deliberately fails OPEN on a missing profile with the reasoning stated in the file. The one unauthenticated action in scope, submitProjectIntakeAction, is unauthenticated by design (it is a public intake) and is covered by ABUSE-PUB-001 for what it lacks INSTEAD of auth, not for lacking auth. LIMB 2, OWNERSHIP AND IDOR — CLEAN. I looked specifically for an id taken from the URL or body and used without an owner predicate, and did not find one in the assigned scope. Every write carries `.eq("artist_id", userId)` (or `.eq("id", userId)` on profiles) in the same statement, not in a preceding read. The service-role uses are the interesting cases and each one was traced: projects.ts runs service-role because RLS 0115 gives the artist SELECT only, and every one of loadProject / setProjectStatusCore / saveProjectNoteCore / linkBookingToProjectCore carries `.eq("artist_id", artistId)` with a rowcount check; booking-form/fields/[id] DELETE uses the service client solely to COUNT booking_requests, and scopes that count to the artist; goods-variants.ts reconcileVariants runs service-role but scopes every update and delete to `.eq("product_id", productId)` after the caller has ownership-checked the product with an RLS read. Three positive defences worth recording because they are easy to get wrong and are right here: goods/actions.ts:326-327 refuses a keep-list image URL that is not already on the product, which blocks a cross-artist graft or delete; travel/studios POST deliberately does not accept the Google Places columns from the body so a crafted request cannot inject a google_maps_url onto a public block; and request/[token] prepareCheckoutAction allowlists every add-on against the artist-confirmed booking_interests rows and caps quantity at what the artist vouched for. LIMB 3, INPUT VALIDATION — sound, with the shape stated. No route uses `await request.json()` output directly in a query. Bodies go through a named validator (normalizeProductInput, normalizeStudioInput, normalizeTripInput, normalizeFieldInput + the shared zod fieldConfigSchema, parseBioPageSettings, parseAppearance, parseConfirmationPage) or through a core that validates. Where coercion is lenient it is deliberate and commented (unrecognised category/status/currency fall back to a safe default, matching the web action). Two fail-closed choices were checked and hold: mobile-goods.ts:103 publishes only on an explicit boolean true, and settings/hub POST refuses a non-object body rather than letting the parser treat it as DEFAULT_BIO_PAGE and wipe the config. UUID_RE guards the path parameter on projects/[id] and booking-form/fields/[id]. LIMB 4, ERROR HANDLING — one finding, OPS-ERR-001. Every route wraps req.json() in try/catch and returns a fixed 400. LIMB 5, ERROR-HANDLING CONSISTENCY — the sibling comparison found real but minor divergence, recorded here rather than as a finding because nothing is unsafe: goods/[id] PUT and goods/[id]/status PATCH both do an explicit existence read and return a structured 404, while booking-form/fields/[id] PATCH does not, so a PATCH naming a non-existent or foreign field id matches zero rows, produces no error and returns 200 {ok:true}. The DELETE verb in that same file DOES return 404. Similarly, mobile goods/discounts PATCH maps every setDiscountActiveCore failure to 500, including the "That code no longer exists." case which is a 404. Neither leaks data or permits a write. LIMB 6, REVALIDATION — one finding, BILL-UI-001, and it is the only mutation in the audited set without one. Counted the other way: 8 collections actions, 2 discounts, 7 goods, 18 studio, 5 bookings/settings, books, appearance, slug (layout-wide), projects, map, and the mobile hub route (which revalidates the PUBLIC /<slug>/hub) all revalidate. | no |
